scenes.visual: Title card 'Two Genes, Two Coins' fades in over a pod holding four kinds of pea. THE WORLD, kept for both chapters (16:9, warm cream background). COLOUR MAP, same in every scene: round copy / round seeds GOLD; wrinkled copy / wrinkled seeds BROWN; yellow copy BRIGHT YELLOW; green copy GREEN; gametes are small white circles (egg) or small white grains (pollen); coin is SILVER. Allele letters (R, r, Y, y) and every number appear only as on-screen text, never spoken. Seeds are simple cartoons, not photographs; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Does a pea hand on its genes one at a time, or in bundles? Chapter one followed one gene, for seed shape. Now add a second, for seed colour.
scenes.caption: Does a pea hand on its genes one at a time, or in bundles? Chapter 1 followed one gene, for seed shape. Now add a second, for seed colour.
scenes.visual: Chapter 1's hybrid plant with its GOLD and BROWN card pair. A second card pair, BRIGHT YELLOW and GREEN, slides in beside it.
scenes.narration: Does a pea hand on its genes one at a time, or in bundles? Chapter 1 followed one gene, for seed shape. Now add a second, for seed colour.

scenes.tts: Mendel crossed a line with round yellow seeds to a line with wrinkled green seeds. Every hybrid seed was round and yellow.
scenes.visual: Left: plant with GOLD round seeds tinted BRIGHT YELLOW, label 'round yellow'. Right: BROWN wrinkled seeds tinted GREEN, label 'wrinkled green'. A cross arrow; the hybrid pod opens to show only round yellow seeds. Label 'RrYy'.
scenes.narration: Mendel crossed a line with round yellow seeds to a line with wrinkled green seeds. Every hybrid seed was round and yellow.

scenes.tts: So the hybrid holds two pairs of cards. A shape pair, one round and one wrinkled. A colour pair, one yellow and one green.
scenes.visual: Inside the hybrid: GOLD + BROWN cards on the left, labelled 'shape'; BRIGHT YELLOW + GREEN cards on the right, labelled 'colour'.
scenes.narration: So the hybrid holds two pairs of cards. A shape pair, one round and one wrinkled. A colour pair, one yellow and one green.

scenes.tts: When it makes an egg or pollen grain, does it toss the two pairs together, or separately?
scenes.visual: Two SILVER coins hover, one over each pair. A question mark sits between them.
scenes.narration: When it makes an egg or pollen grain, does it toss the two pairs together, or separately?

scenes.tts: Suppose they were glued together. Round and yellow came in from one parent, so they would leave together. The hybrid would make only two kinds of gamete.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis A panel, labelled 'glued together': the GOLD and YELLOW cards are clipped as one; the BROWN and GREEN cards as another. One coin flips; gametes fill a tray with only two kinds, half each: 'RY' and 'ry'.
scenes.narration: Suppose they were glued together. Round and yellow came in from one parent, so they would leave together. The hybrid would make only two kinds of gamete.

scenes.tts: Now suppose each pair has its own coin. Any shape card can go with any colour card. The hybrid would make four kinds of gamete, a quarter each.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis B panel, labelled 'separate coins': two coins flip independently; the tray fills with four kinds in equal numbers: 'RY', 'Ry', 'rY', 'ry', each '1/4'. Panels A and B now sit side by side.
scenes.narration: Now suppose each pair has its own coin. Any shape card can go with any colour card. The hybrid would make four kinds of gamete, a quarter each.

scenes.tts: A selfed seed mixes two of the hybrid's gametes, and dominance hides some copies. So how could you read the hybrid's gametes directly?
scenes.visual: Both panels dim slightly. A single round yellow seed sits in the centre with two faint card pairs behind it, unlabelled. Question card: 'How could you read the hybrid's gametes?'
scenes.narration: A selfed seed mixes two of the hybrid's gametes, and dominance hides some copies. So how could you read the hybrid's gametes directly?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Cross the hybrid to a wrinkled green plant. That tester can only give wrinkled and green copies. So each seed shows which copies the hybrid gave it.
scenes.visual: A wrinkled green plant appears, labelled 'tester rryy'; its gamete tray holds only BROWN+GREEN gametes. Each hybrid gamete joins a tester gamete, and the seed that forms takes the look of the hybrid's cards. Label 'each seed reads one hybrid gamete'.
scenes.narration: Cross the hybrid to a wrinkled green plant. That tester can only give wrinkled and green copies. So each seed shows which copies the hybrid gave it.

scenes.tts: Mendel ran this cross with the hybrid as the seed parent. The seeds fell into four kinds, in roughly equal numbers.
scenes.visual: Four trays labelled 'round yellow', 'round green', 'wrinkled yellow', 'wrinkled green'. Seeds drop into them and bars rise to 31, 26, 27, 26 (numbers on screen) on a count axis. Label 'hybrid as seed parent (eggs), 110 seeds'. A WHITE dashed line marks one quarter of 110: 27.5 (computed).
scenes.narration: Mendel ran this cross with the hybrid as the seed parent. The seeds fell into four kinds, in roughly equal numbers.

scenes.tts: Then he ran it the other way, with the hybrid as the pollen parent. Again, four kinds, roughly equal.
scenes.visual: A second set of four bars rises beside the first on the same count axis: 24, 25, 22, 27. Label 'hybrid as pollen parent, 98 seeds'. This set gets its own WHITE dashed line at one quarter of 98: 24.5 (computed).
scenes.narration: Then he ran it the other way, with the hybrid as the pollen parent. Again, four kinds, roughly equal.

scenes.tts: So eggs and pollen alike carried all four combinations about equally. Fully glued pairs cannot do that. Two separate coins can.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis A panel fades with a soft cross over it; Hypothesis B panel slides beside the two bar sets and brightens. Text: 'four kinds, about equal, eggs and pollen alike'.
scenes.narration: So eggs and pollen alike carried all four combinations about equally. Fully glued pairs cannot do that. Two separate coins can.

scenes.tts: Now let the double hybrid pollinate itself, as Mendel did. Separate coins predict how its seeds should split.
scenes.visual: The hybrid self-pollinates; a pile of round and wrinkled, yellow and green seeds pours out. Text: '556 seeds from 15 F1 plants'.
scenes.narration: Now let the double hybrid pollinate itself, as Mendel did. Separate coins predict how its seeds should split.

scenes.tts: Draw a square for all the seeds. Shape cuts it into three quarters round and one quarter wrinkled. Colour cuts it the other way.
scenes.visual: A square. A vertical line splits it 3/4 (GOLD, 'round') to 1/4 (BROWN, 'wrinkled'). Then a horizontal line splits it 3/4 (BRIGHT YELLOW, 'yellow') to 1/4 (GREEN, 'green'). Fractions on screen.
scenes.narration: Draw a square for all the seeds. Shape cuts it into three quarters round and one quarter wrinkled. Colour cuts it the other way.

scenes.tts: Separate coins multiply, so each box's share is a product. The round yellow corner is the biggest. The wrinkled green corner is the smallest.
scenes.visual: The four rectangles light up with their areas as text: 9/16 round yellow, 3/16 round green, 3/16 wrinkled yellow, 1/16 wrinkled green. Under it: '3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16' as on-screen text only.
scenes.narration: Separate coins multiply, so each box's share is a product. The round yellow corner is the biggest. The wrinkled green corner is the smallest.

scenes.tts: Mendel's counts sat close to those shares. Close, but not exact, as real counts usually are.
scenes.visual: Beside the square, four pairs of bars: counted 315, 108, 101, 32 next to expected 312.75, 104.25, 104.25, 34.75 (computed). Text: '9 : 3 : 3 : 1'.
scenes.narration: Mendel's counts sat close to those shares. Close, but not exact, as real counts usually are.

scenes.tts: This held for seed shape and seed colour. It does not hold for every pair of genes. Why not comes in a later lesson.
scenes.visual: The square shrinks to a corner. Two other card pairs appear with a faint clip between them and a label 'not every pair: later lesson'. No data shown.
scenes.narration: This held for seed shape and seed colour. It does not hold for every pair of genes. Why not comes in a later lesson.

scenes.tts: So here is the whole idea. Two copies of each gene, and one goes to each gamete by a coin toss. Genes that assort independently are separate coins, like seed shape and colour.
scenes.visual: Both card pairs and both coins line up. The sentences appear one at a time beside them.
scenes.narration: So here is the whole idea. Two copies of each gene, and one goes to each gamete by a coin toss. Genes that assort independently are separate coins, like seed shape and colour.

scenes.visual: End card, large text centred: 'Genes that assort independently are separate coins: their chances multiply.'
